Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Nahl (The Bee), because it mentions the wondrous qualities of the bee, which point to the marvellous craftsmanship of the Creator. The bee is not mentioned in any other surah.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Mentioning the signs of creation in the cosmos. The surah draws attention to the power of Allah, the One, the Subduer. It gathers what is in the universe: heavens and earth, sun and moon, night and day, mountains and seas, plants and fruits. It presents these before the eyes, uncovered and perceptible, so that the beholder becomes certain that every atom in it bears witness to Divine Oneness. All of this serves to establish the power of Allah, which indicates that He alone deserves worship, to the exclusion of anything else.

• Reminding of the Creator, the Benefactor, whose blessings cannot be counted and whose bounties cannot be exhausted. It draws a comparison between Him and false deities, and sets forth parables depicting the condition of the alleged deities that possess nothing.

• Warning against what befell the nations that associated partners with Allah and denied His messengers, and contrasting this with the opposite: the bliss of the God-fearing who are patient under the harm of the polytheists, and who emigrated in the way of Allah to defend monotheism.

• Explaining the wisdom behind the creation of some creatures and their benefits, the great blessings they hold for humankind, and the lessons and signs contained in their creation and subjugation.

• Extolling the Qur'an (al-Qur'an), declaring it free from the approach of Satan (al-Shaytan), warning against falling into his snares, and refuting the fabrications of the polytheists against the Book of Allah.

• Commanding fundamental principles of the Shari'ah in dealings, such as justice and excellence (ihsan), spending and comforting the needy, fulfilling covenants, and forbidding indecency, evil, oppression and breaking of agreements, along with the great recompense that follows from this in this world and the Hereafter.

[The Tafsir]

The Hour has drawn near, and Allah's decree of punishment for you, O disbelievers, is close at hand. So do not seek to hasten the punishment in mockery of the Messenger's threat to you. Allah, glorified and exalted, is far above association and partners.

God sends down the angels with the revelation by His command, upon whomever He wills of His servants, the messengers: "Warn people against associating others with Me, and that there is no deity worthy of worship except Me, so fear Me by performing My obligations and devoting worship to Me alone, sincerely."

God created the heavens and the earth with truth, so that His servants might take them as evidence of the greatness of their Creator, and that He alone is deserving of worship. He is exalted and high above the partners they associate with Him.

He created man from a despised fluid, and then he becomes strong and deluded. So he grows extremely contentious and disputes with his Lord, denying the resurrection and other matters, such as His saying: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ and he forgets God, who created him from nothing.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 5:

And the livestock—camels, cattle, and sheep and goats—He created for you, O people, and He placed in their wool, their fur, and their hair warmth, and other benefits in their milk, their hides, and their riding, and from them you eat.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 6:

For you in them is beauty that brings joy to you when you bring them back to their pens in the evening, and when you lead them out to pasture in the morning.

And these cattle carry your heavy loads to a distant land that you could not have reached except with great effort from yourselves and severe hardship. Indeed, your Lord is truly merciful to you, with abundant mercy, in your present life and your life to come; for He has subjected to you what you need, so to Him belongs all praise and all thanks.

And He created horses, mules, and donkeys for you, so that you may ride them, and as adornment and a beautiful sight for you. And He creates for you other means of transport and more, of which you have no knowledge, so that you may increase in faith in Him and in gratitude to Him.

Upon Allah is the explanation of the straight path for your guidance, and it is Islam. Among the paths, some are crooked and do not lead to guidance; these are every creed and sect (milal wa-nihal) that opposes Islam. And if Allah had willed your guidance, He would have guided you all to faith.

He is the One who sent down for you water from the clouds: from it you have drink, and by it He brings forth for you plants in which your livestock graze. Through them your animals give you milk and other benefits.

It brings forth for you from the earth, by this one water, crops of various kinds, and with it olives, date palms, and grapes, and with it every kind of fruit. Indeed, in that bringing forth is a clear sign for a people who reflect, so that they take heed.

And He subjected to you the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who use their reason.

Wait, that is not a faithful rendering. Here is the complete translation:

He subjected to you the night for your rest, and the day for your livelihood, and He subjected to you the sun as a light, and the moon as a light, and for knowing the years and the reckoning, and other benefits. And the stars in the sky are subjected to you by the command of Allah, for knowing the times, and for knowing the time of the ripening of fruits and crops, and for guidance by them in darkness. Indeed, in that subjection are clear signs for a people who understand from Allah His proofs and evidences.

And He has subjected to you whatever He created for you on the earth of various kinds: its animals, fruits, and minerals, and other things whose colors and benefits differ. Indeed, in that creation and in the variation of colors and benefits there is a lesson for a people who take heed, and who know that in the subjection of these things there are signs of the oneness of Allah the Exalted and of His being singled out for worship.

He it is who subjected the sea to you, that you may eat from it fresh flesh (of fish) that you catch, and extract from it ornaments that you wear, such as pearls and coral. And you see the great ships ploughing through it, going and coming, and you ride them, so that you may seek God's bounty through trade and the profit gained therein, and perhaps you will give thanks to God Most High for His great favour upon you, and so not worship other than Him.

He cast firmly into the earth mountains that hold it steady so that it does not shift with you, and He made in it rivers for you to drink from, and He made in it roads so that you may find your way by them to the places you intend to reach.

The commentary text is: "And He placed in the earth landmarks by which you find your way on roads by day, just as He placed the stars for guidance by night."

Translation:

And He placed in the earth landmarks by which you find your way on the roads by day, just as He placed the stars for guidance by night.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 17:

Do you then make Allah, who creates all these things and others, equal in deserving worship to the supposed deities, which create nothing? Will you not then remember the greatness of Allah, so that you single Him out for worship?

And if you try to count the blessings of Allah upon you, you will not be able to enumerate them, because of their abundance and their variety. Indeed, Allah is Most Forgiving to you and Most Merciful to you, for He overlooks your shortcomings in giving thanks for the blessings, does not withdraw them from you because of your negligence, and does not hasten punishment upon you.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 16, Verse 19:

Allah, glory be to Him, knows all your deeds, whether you conceal them within your souls or display them to others, and He will recompense you for them.
The gods that the polytheists worship create nothing, even if it is small. They are created things that the disbelievers fashioned with their own hands, so how can they worship them?

They are all inanimate objects, with no life in them, and they do not perceive the time at which God raises up their worshippers. They will be with them, so that they will all be thrown into the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

Your God, the One deserving worship alone, is Allah, the one God. As for those who do not believe in the Resurrection, their hearts deny His oneness, glorified be He, because they do not fear His punishment; so they are arrogant toward accepting the truth and toward worshipping Allah alone.

Indeed, Allah knows what they conceal of beliefs, statements and deeds, and what they display of them, and He will recompense them for that. Indeed He, the Mighty and Majestic, does not love those who are arrogant towards His worship and submission to Him, and He will recompense them for that.

When these polytheists were asked about what was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), they said, falsely and deceitfully: "He has brought nothing but the tales of the earlier peoples and their falsehoods."

Their end will be that they will bear their sins in full on the Day of Resurrection, none of them being forgiven, and they will also bear the sins of those they misled, who were deceived by them, turning them away from Islam, without any reduction from their own sins. Surely evil is what they bear as sin.

The unbelievers before these polytheists had already plotted against their messengers and against the truth they brought. So God's command came upon their structure from its foundation and base, and the roof fell down on them from above, and destruction came upon them from where they felt safe, from a direction they did not expect or anticipate it would come from.

Then on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will disgrace them with punishment and humiliate them through it, and He will say: "Where are My partners, the deities you used to worship besides Me, that they might ward off the punishment from you? You used to fight against the prophets and the believers and oppose them on their account?" The righteous scholars said: The humiliation on this day and the punishment are for the disbelievers in Allah and His messengers, those whose souls the angels take while they are wronging themselves through disbelief. Then they submit to the command of Allah when they see death, and they deny what they used to worship besides Allah, and they say: "We did not do any wrong deeds." It will be said to them: "You have lied; indeed you used to do them. Surely Allah is All-Knowing of all your deeds, and He will recompense you for them."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 30:

When it is said to the believers who fear Allah: "What has Allah sent down upon the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?" they say: "Allah has sent down goodness and guidance." ﴿For those who believed in Allah and His Messenger in this world, and who called the servants of Allah to faith and righteous deeds, there is a great reward of victory for them in this world and abundant provision; and the Abode of the Hereafter is better for them and greater than what they were given in this world. And excellent indeed is the Abode of the Hereafter for those who feared Allah in this world, so they guarded against His punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.﴾

Just as these (disbelievers of Makkah) denied, the disbelievers before them denied, so Allah destroyed them. The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 35:

The polytheists said: "Had Allah willed that we worship Him alone, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our forefathers before us, nor would we have declared unlawful anything He had not made unlawful." With this same false argument, the disbelievers before them argued, and they were lying. For Allah commanded them and forbade them, and enabled them to carry out what He had enjoined upon them, and He gave them a power and a will from which their actions proceed. Therefore their argument from divine decree and predestination is among the most baseless of falsehoods, coming after the warning of the messengers to them. The messengers who warn them have no duty except the clear delivery of what they were commanded to convey.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 36:

And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying]: "Worship Allah alone and shun the false deities (al-taghut)," meaning the devils, the idols, the dead, and whatever else is taken as a protector besides Allah. Among them were those whom Allah guided, and they followed the messengers. And among them was the obstinate one who followed the path of error, so misguidance was decreed upon him, and Allah did not grant him success. So travel through the earth and observe with your own eyes how the end of those who denied was, and what destruction befell them, so that you may take heed.

If you, O Messenger, exert your utmost effort to guide these polytheists, know that Allah does not guide whoever He leaves to stray, and they have no one besides Allah to help them or to ward off His punishment from them.

These disbelievers swore by God with emphatic oaths that God would not resurrect those who die, after they have decayed and scattered. Yes, indeed, God will surely resurrect them; it is a promise binding upon Him, a true promise. But most people do not know God's power to resurrect, so they deny it.

God will resurrect all of His servants, in order to make clear to them the reality of the resurrection about which they disagreed, and so that the disbelievers who deny it may know that they were upon falsehood, and that they were lying when they swore that there would be no resurrection.

The commentary on Surah 16, verse 40:

Indeed, the matter of resurrection is easy for Us. When We want a thing, We only say to it, "Be," and it immediately exists.

Those who emigrated for the sake of Allah after they had been wronged, We will surely settle them in this world in a good dwelling; and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, because their reward there is Paradise. If those who stayed behind from emigration knew with certain knowledge what Allah has of reward for those who emigrate in His cause, not one of them would have remained behind from it.

These are the emigrants who strove for the sake of Allah: they are the ones who were patient in obeying Allah's commands and in refraining from His prohibitions, and patient under His painful decrees; and upon their Lord alone do they rely. Therefore they deserved this great station.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 43:

We did not send before you (O Messenger) any messengers except men, not angels, to whom We revealed. And if you (O polytheists of Quraysh) do not believe this, then ask the scholars of the previous scriptures, and they will inform you that the prophets were humans, if you do not know that they were human. The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 50:

The angels fear their Lord, who is above them in His essence, His dominance, and the perfection of His attributes, and they do what they are commanded to do of obedience to Allah. In the verse is an affirmation of the attribute of highness and of being above for Allah over all of His creation, as befits His majesty and perfection.
God said to His servants: "Do not worship two gods. Your object of worship is only one God, so fear Me alone, and none other than Me."

To Allah belongs everything in the heavens and the earth, by creation, ownership, and servitude. And to Him alone belong worship, obedience, and sincere devotion, always. Is it fitting for you to fear other than Allah and to worship Him?

Whatever blessing you have, whether guidance, health of body, abundance of provision, children, or other things, it comes from Allah alone; He is the One who bestows it upon you. Then, when illness, affliction, or drought befalls you, to Allah alone you turn in earnest supplication, crying out to Him.

Then, when He removes from you the affliction and the sickness, behold, a group of you who, toward their Lord, the Bestower of favor who granted them deliverance, take partners and allies alongside Him.

So that they may deny Our blessings upon them, among which is the removal of affliction from them. So enjoy your worldly life, but its end is to vanish, and you will soon know the consequence of your disbelief and disobedience.

Among the ugly deeds of the polytheists is that they assign a portion of their wealth, which God has provided for them, to the idols they have taken as gods—idols that know nothing, neither benefit nor harm—seeking nearness to them. ﴿By God, you will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what you used to fabricate of falsehood against God.﴾

They attribute daughters to Allah, glory be to Him, while for themselves they choose the sons they desire. The disbelievers say, "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Allah is exalted above their statement.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 58:

When one of them is given news of the birth of a female, his face darkens, and he is filled with grief and sorrow, out of aversion to what he has heard.

He hides from his people, out of dislike of meeting them while burdened with what distresses him of grief and shame, because of the girl who has been born to him, and he is perplexed about this newborn: will he keep her alive in humiliation and disgrace, or bury her alive in the dust? Certainly evil is the judgment they have made, in assigning daughters to Allah and sons to themselves.

For those who do not believe in the Hereafter and do not work for it, is the evil attribute: weakness, need, ignorance, and disbelief. And to Allah belong the highest attributes: perfection and independence from His creation. He is the Almighty in His dominion, the All-Wise in His management.

If Allah were to hold people accountable for their disbelief and their fabrication, He would not leave a single living creature on the earth. But He gives them respite until a specified time, the end of their lifespans. When their term comes, they cannot be delayed from it even for a brief moment, nor can they advance it.

Among their abominable acts: they attribute to Allah what they themselves dislike, namely daughters, while their tongues falsely claim that they will have the good end. Truly, for them is the Fire, and they will be left behind and forgotten in it.

By Allah, We certainly sent messengers to nations before you, O Messenger, but Satan made their deeds, of disbelief, denial, and worship of other than Allah, appear attractive to them. So he is their ally (in misguidance) in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a painful, afflicting punishment.

We did not send down the Qur'an to you, O Messenger, except that you might make clear to people that about which they have differed concerning religion and its rulings; so that the proof may be established against them by your clear explanation, which leaves no path for falsehood into souls, and because the Qur'an is guidance that leaves no room for bewilderment, and a mercy for the believers in their following of guidance and their avoidance of misguidance.

And Allah sends down rain from the clouds, and by it brings forth vegetation from the earth after it had been barren and dry. Indeed, in the sending down of rain and the growth of plants there is surely a sign of Allah's power to resurrect and of His oneness, for a people who listen, reflect, obey Allah, and fear Him.

Indeed, for you, O people, in the cattle (al-an'am), which are camels, cows and sheep, there is a lesson. You have seen that We give you to drink from their udders milk that comes out from between waste matter (al-farth), which is what is in the stomach (al-karish), and blood, pure and free of every impurity, pleasant, such that no one who drinks it chokes on it.

And from Our blessings upon you are the fruits of the date palms and grapevines, from which you take intoxicants (khamr) and wholesome provision. Indeed, in this is a sign of Allah's power for a people who reason, who consider the proofs and take lessons from them.

And among Our blessings upon you are the fruits of the date palms and grapes, from which you make an intoxicant (khamr) — this was before its prohibition — and good provision. Indeed, in what has been mentioned is a clear sign of Allah's power for a people who use their reason, who consider the proofs and take lessons from them.
And your Lord inspired the bee, O Messenger, saying: "Make for yourselves houses in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what people build of buildings and roofs."

Then eat from every kind of fruit, and follow the paths of your Lord made easy for you, to seek provision in the mountains and among the trees, and He has made them easy for you so that you do not go astray in returning to them, even if they are far away. From the bellies of the bees there comes out honey of varying colors, white, yellow, red, and other than these, in which there is healing for people from illnesses. Indeed, in what the bees produce there is a strong proof of the power of their Creator for a people who reflect, so that they may take heed.

Allah the Almighty created you, then causes you to die at the end of your lifespans. Among you is one who is returned to the most wretched age, which is senility, so that he is like he was in childhood, knowing nothing of what he once knew. Indeed Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful: His knowledge and power encompass everything. The One who returned a person to this state is able to cause him to die and then resurrect him.

God has favored some of you over others in provision in this world. Some of you are rich and some are poor; some of you own property and some are owned. So those who own do not give their slaves from what God has given them such that they would become partners with them, equal to them in wealth. If they would not accept this for themselves, then why do they accept to make partners for God from among His servants? Indeed, this is among the greatest wrongdoing and ingratitude for the blessings of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Allah, glory be to Him, made for you spouses from your own kind, so that your souls might find rest with them, and He made for you, through them, children, and from their offspring grandchildren, and He provided you with good things of sustenance: fruits, grains, meat, and other things. Do they then believe in the falsehood of their partners' divinity, and deny the blessings of Allah which cannot be counted, and not give thanks to Him by devoting worship exclusively to Him, He who is exalted and majestic?

The idolaters worship idols that cannot give them any provision from the heavens, such as rain, nor from the earth, such as crops. They possess nothing, and it is not possible for them to possess anything, because they have no power.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 74:

Now that you know that idols and images cannot benefit you, do not, O people, set up for God equals, peers from among His creation, whom you associate with Him in worship. Indeed, God knows what you do, while you are heedless and do not know your error and the evil of your end.

God set forth an example to show the corruption of the belief of the people of polytheism: a man who is a slave, incapable of acting freely and owning nothing, and another man who is free, who has lawful wealth that God has provided him, who has the power to dispose of it and gives from it secretly and openly. Would any sensible person say that the two men are equal? Likewise, God, the Creator, the Owner, the One who disposes of all affairs, is not equal to His creation and His servants, so how do you make them equal? ﴿All praise is due to God﴾ alone, for He alone deserves praise and commendation. Rather, most of the polytheists do not know that praise and blessing belong to God, and that He alone deserves to be worshipped.

And God presents another parable, illustrating the falsehood of polytheism: two men. One of them is mute and deaf, unable to understand or make himself understood, unable to benefit himself or others. He is a heavy burden on whoever is responsible for him and supports him: when sent on some matter that needs attending to, he does not succeed, and nothing good comes back to him. The other man has sound faculties, benefits himself and others, enjoins justice, and is on a clear path with no crookedness in it. Would the two men be considered equal in the view of sensible people? So how can you equate the mute, deaf idol with God, the Almighty who bestows every good?

To Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, belongs knowledge of the unseen in the heavens and the earth, and the matter of the Hour in its swiftness of coming is nothing but like a quick glance of the eye, or even faster than that. Indeed, Allah is over all things Competent.

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, brought you forth from your mothers' wombs after the term of pregnancy, while you knew nothing of what was around you. He made for you the means of perception: hearing, sight and hearts, so that you might give thanks to Allah, exalted is He, for those blessings, and single Him out, mighty and majestic is He, in worship.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 16, verse 79:**

Have the polytheists not considered the birds, made subservient for flight in the air between the sky and the earth by Allah's command? Nothing holds them up from falling except Him, glory be to Him, through the wings and tails He created for them and the ability He gave them to do so. Indeed, in this subjugation and holding aloft are signs for a people who believe in what they see of the proofs of Allah's power.

Allah, glorified is He, made for you, from your houses, a place of rest and stability with your families while you are residing in settled areas. And for you, during your travels, He made tents and domes from the hides of livestock, which are light for you to carry when you journey and light for you to pitch when you stop and settle after travelling. And from the wool of sheep, the fur of camels, and the hair of goats He made for you furnishings: coverings, garments, blankets, rugs, and adornments, which you enjoy for a specified term and a known time.

God has made for you shade from trees and other things, and He has made for you, in the mountains, caves and hollows as places to take refuge in when you need them. He has made for you garments of cotton, wool and other materials, which protect you from heat and cold, and He has made for you iron, which wards off stabbing and harm in your battles. Just as Allah has bestowed these blessings upon you, so He completes His favour upon you by making clear the true religion, so that you may submit to the command of Allah alone and not associate anything with Him in His worship.

If they turn away from you, O Messenger, after having seen the signs, then do not grieve. Your duty is only to convey the clear message with which you were sent, and as for guidance, it rests with Us.

These polytheists recognize God's blessing upon them in sending Muhammad (ﷺ) to them, and yet they deny his prophethood, and most of his people are among those who deny his prophethood, not among those who affirm it.

Mention to them, O Messenger, what will happen on the Day of Resurrection, when We raise up from every nation its messenger as a witness over the faith of whoever believed among them and the disbelief of whoever disbelieved. Then those who disbelieved will not be permitted to offer excuses for what they committed, nor will they be asked to appease their Lord through repentance and righteous deeds, for the time for that has already passed.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, a simplified tafsir (exegesis) of the Qur'an) on Surah 16, verse 85:

﴿And when those who disbelieved see the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter, its severity will not be lightened for them at all, nor will they be given respite, nor will their punishment be delayed.﴾

When the polytheists see on the Day of Resurrection the deities they worshipped besides Allah, they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to worship besides You." Then the deities will refute those who worshipped them, and say: "Indeed you, O polytheists, are liars, when you made us partners with Allah and worshipped us along with Him. We did not command you to do that, nor did we claim that we deserve divinity; so the blame is upon you."

The polytheists will display submission and humility before Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and whatever falsehoods they used to fabricate, such as that their deities would intercede for them, will vanish from them.

Those who disbelieved in the Oneness of Allah and in your prophethood, O Messenger, and denied you, and who barred others from believing in Allah and His Messenger, We will increase their punishment upon their disbelief and a punishment for their turning people away from following the truth. This is because of their deliberate corruption and their misguiding of the servants of Allah through disbelief and disobedience.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 89:

Mention, O Messenger, the time when We will raise up on the Day of Resurrection, in every nation of the nations, a witness over them, who is the messenger whom Allah sent to them from among themselves and in their tongue. And We bring you, O Messenger, as a witness over your nation, that you conveyed the message of your Lord. We have sent down to you the Qur'an as an explanation of every matter that needs clarification, such as the rulings of the lawful and the unlawful, reward and punishment, and other things; and it is a guidance from misguidance, and a mercy for those who believe in it and act upon it, and a glad tidings of good outcome for the believers.

Indeed, Allah, glorified and exalted, commands His servants in this Qur'an to be just and equitable in regard to His right, by affirming His oneness (tawhid) and not associating anything with Him, and in regard to the rights of His servants, by giving every person with a right his due. He commands excellence (ihsan) in regard to His right, by worshipping Him and performing His obligations in the lawful manner prescribed, and toward creation in words and deeds. He commands giving to those of kinship what maintains their ties and kindness to them, and He forbids everything that is ugly in speech or action, and what the Sharia rejects and does not approve of, such as disbelief and acts of disobedience, and wronging people and transgressing against them. And Allah, by this command and this prohibition, admonishes you and reminds you of the consequences, so that you may remember the commands of Allah and benefit from them.

Fulfil every covenant you have bound yourselves to, whether between you and God, the Exalted, or between you and people, provided it does not contradict the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet. Do not break your oaths after you have confirmed them, for you have made God a guarantor and surety over you when you made the covenant with Him. Indeed, God knows what you do, and He will recompense you for it.

Do not go back on your oaths after you have confirmed them, for your situation would be like that of a woman who spun her yarn and made it firm, then unravelled it. You make your oaths, which you swore when you made the pact, a means of deceiving those with whom you made it, and you break your covenant whenever you find a group that has more wealth and benefit than those you made it with. Allah is only testing you by what He has commanded you of fulfilling covenants and by what He has forbidden you of breaking them. On the Day of Resurrection He will surely make clear to you that about which you used to differ in the world: belief in Allah and the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

If God had willed, He would have guided you all together and made you one community upon a single religion, which is Islam and faith, and compelled you to it. But He leads astray whom He wills, of those whom He knows to prefer error, so He does not guide them, in His justice; and He guides whom He wills, of those whom He knows to prefer the truth, so He grants them success, in His bounty. And you will surely be called to account by God, all of you, on the Day of Resurrection, for what you used to do in the world, regarding what He commanded you and what He forbade you, and He will recompense you for that.

Do not make your oaths a means of deception between you, lest a foot slip after it has been firmly planted, and you taste evil (punishment) for having barred others from the way of Allah, and you will have a great punishment in the Hereafter.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 95:

Do not break your covenant with God in order to exchange it for a small gain from the goods of this world. What God has of reward for fulfilling the covenant is far better for you than this small price, if you are people of knowledge. So reflect on the difference between the two goods of this world and the Hereafter.

What you have of the fleeting goods of this world will pass away, but what Allah has of provision and reward for you does not cease. We will surely reward those who endured the hardships of the obligations, among them fulfilling the covenant, with the reward for their best deeds. So We give them for the least of their deeds just as We give for the greatest, out of bounty.

Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer in Allah and His Messenger, We will surely grant a good and contented life in this world, even if they have little wealth. And We will surely reward them in the Hereafter with their recompense according to the best of what they did in this world.

If you, believer, wish to recite any part of the Qur'an, then seek refuge in Allah from the evil of Satan, the one cast out from the mercy of Allah, saying: "I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed."

This passage is a tafsir commentary on Qur'an 16:99–100, so the Qur'anic quotations would normally appear in ﴿ ﴾ markers. However, the text given here is the commentary itself and contains no direct Qur'anic quotation, so no ﴿ ﴾ markers are needed.

Translation:

Indeed, Satan has no authority over those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and upon their Lord alone do they rely. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and obey him, and those who, because of their obedience to him, are polytheists associating others with Allah, exalted is He.

Translation:

Indeed, Satan has no authority over those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and upon their Lord alone do they rely. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and obey him, and those who, because of their obedience to him, are polytheists associating others with Allah, exalted is He.

When We substitute one verse for another—and Allah, the Creator, knows best what benefits His creation—by sending down rulings at different times, the disbelievers say: "You, O Muhammad, are merely a liar, fabricating against Allah what He did not say." But Muhammad ﷺ is not as they claim. Rather, most of them have no knowledge of their Lord or of His law and its rulings.

Say to them, O Messenger: The Qur'an is not something I have invented. Rather, Jibril (Gabriel) brought it down from your Lord with truth and justice, to strengthen the believers, to guide them away from misguidance, and as good tidings for those who submit and humble themselves before Allah, Lord of the worlds.

And We certainly know that the disbelievers say, "He is only being taught by a human being." They are lying. The tongue of the one they attribute this teaching to is foreign and not clear, while the Qur'an is in Arabic, extremely clear and plain. (ﷺ)

The commentary on surah 16, verse 104:

"Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Qur'an, Allah does not guide them to the right path, and they will have a painful, grievous punishment in the Hereafter."

Only those who do not believe in God and His signs fabricate lies, and those are the liars in their claim. As for Muhammad (ﷺ), who believes in his Lord and submits to Him, it is impossible for him to lie about God or to attribute to Him what He has not said.

Only those who utter the word of disbelief and renounce faith after having believed fabricate lies. Upon them is wrath from Allah, except one who is forced to utter disbelief while his heart remains firm in faith. He bears no blame. But whoever utters disbelief and his heart is content with it, upon them is severe wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment. That is because they preferred the worldly life and its adornment over the Hereafter and its reward, and because Allah does not grant success to the disbelievers in reaching the truth and what is right.

Only those who utter the word of disbelief and renounce faith after having believed fabricate lies. Upon them is wrath from Allah, except one who is forced to utter disbelief while his heart remains firm in faith. He bears no blame. But whoever utters disbelief and his heart is content with it, upon them is severe wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment. That is because they preferred the worldly life and its adornment over the Hereafter and its reward, and because Allah does not grant success to the disbelievers in reaching the truth and what is right.

Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts with disbelief and their preference of the worldly life over the Hereafter, so that the light of guidance cannot reach them. He has made their hearing deaf to the signs of Allah, so they do not hear them with contemplation, and He has blinded their sight, so they do not see the proofs that indicate the divinity of Allah. And those are the heedless ones, unaware of the punishment that Allah has prepared for them.
Truly, they are the losers in the Hereafter, the ruined, those who spent their lives on that which brings about their own punishment and destruction.

Then indeed your Lord, for those who were oppressed in Makkah, who were tormented by the polytheists until they went along with them in outward appearance, so that they were tempted into uttering what pleased them while their hearts were content with faith, and when they were able to escape, they emigrated to Madinah, then they strove in the cause of Allah and endured the hardships of the obligations—indeed your Lord, after their repentance, is Forgiving toward them and Merciful to them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 111:

And remind them, O Messenger, of the Day of Resurrection, when every soul will come pleading on its own behalf, offering every kind of excuse, and Allah will fully repay every soul for what it has done, without any injustice to it. He will not increase them in punishment, nor will He diminish their reward.

This is a commentary text from the Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex), on surah 16, verse 112.

God struck an example: a town, "Makkah," which was secure from attack and at peace, free from straitened living; its provision came to it abundantly and easily from every direction. But its people denied the blessings of God upon them, associated others with Him, and did not give Him thanks. So God punished them with hunger and with fear of the expeditions and armies of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), which were frightening them. That was because of their disbelief and their false deeds.

And Allah sent to the people of Makkah a messenger from among them, namely the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), whose lineage, truthfulness, and trustworthiness they knew. Yet they did not accept what he brought them, and they did not believe him. So the punishment seized them through hardships, hunger, fear, and the killing of their leaders at Badr, while they were wronging themselves by associating partners with Allah and by barring others from His path.

So eat, O believers, of what Allah has provided for you, which He has made lawful and wholesome, and be thankful for Allah's blessing upon you by acknowledging it and spending it in obedience to Allah, if you are truly devoted to His command, listening and obeying Him, worshipping Him alone, with no partner.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 115:

Indeed, Allah has only forbidden you carrion, blood poured forth from the slaughtered animal at the time of its slaughter, the flesh of swine, and that over which other than Allah has been invoked. But whoever is compelled by necessity, fearing death, to eat any of these forbidden things, while being neither disobedient nor exceeding the limit of necessity, then indeed Allah is Forgiving toward him and Merciful to him; He will not punish him for what he did.

And do not say, O polytheists, concerning the lie that your tongues describe: "This is lawful" for what Allah has forbidden, and "This is unlawful" for what Allah has made lawful, so that you may fabricate lies against Allah by attributing lawfulness and unlawfulness to Him. Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not attain any good, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.
"Their enjoyment in this world is a fleeting, meager enjoyment, and for them in the Hereafter there is a painful torment."

And for the Jews We made unlawful what We have already told you about, O Messenger: every animal with claws (ẓufur), and the fat of cattle and sheep, except what their backs or their intestines carry, or what is mixed with bone. We did not wrong them by making that unlawful for them; rather, they were wrongdoers against their own souls through disbelief and transgression, and so they deserved the prohibition as a punishment for them.

Then indeed your Lord, for those who committed evil deeds in a state of ignorance (of their consequence, and that they necessitate the wrath of God), and out of heedlessness on their part or weakness of certainty, then every disobeyer of God, whether in error or deliberately, is in this respect ignorant, even if he knows that it is forbidden, then they turned back to God from the sins they had been upon, and set right their souls and their deeds. Indeed your Lord, after their repentance and their setting things right, is Forgiving toward them and Merciful to them.

Indeed, Ibrahim (Abraham) was an imam (a leader and exemplar) in goodness, and he was obedient and submissive to Allah, not inclining away from the religion of Islam, believing in the Oneness of Allah and not associating anything with Him. He was thankful for the blessings Allah bestowed upon him. Allah chose him for His message and guided him to the straight path, which is Islam. We gave him in this world a good reputation, a commendation from people among later generations, and an example to follow, as well as righteous offspring. And indeed, in the Hereafter, he is with Allah among the righteous, those who hold high ranks.

Then We revealed to you, O Messenger, that you should follow the religion of Islam as Ibrahim followed it, and that you should remain steadfast upon it and not deviate from it, for Ibrahim was not one of those who associate partners with Allah, besides Him.

This is the commentary on Surah an-Nahl (16), verse 124, from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

The sanctity of the Sabbath (Yawm as-Sabt), devoting oneself to worship on it, was only imposed upon the Jews, who disagreed about it with their prophet, and chose it instead of Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah), which they had been commanded to honour. And indeed your Lord, O Messenger, will judge between those who differed over it, concerning what they disagreed about with their prophet, on the Day of Resurrection, and will recompense each one according to what they deserve.

Call (people), O Messenger, you and those who follow you, to the religion of your Lord and His straight path, with wisdom (al-hikmah) that Allah has revealed to you in the Book and the Sunnah, and address the people in the manner suitable to them, and advise them with good advice that encourages them toward good and warns them away from evil, and argue with them in the best manner of argument, with gentleness and kindness. Your duty is only to convey (the message), and you have conveyed it. As for their guidance, it rests with Allah alone; He knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best who are guided.

If you, believers, wish to retaliate against those who have wronged you, then do not exceed what they did to you. But if you are patient, it is truly better for you: in this world through victory, and in the Hereafter through a great reward.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 16, verse 127:

Be patient, O Messenger, over the harm that has befallen you for the sake of Allah, until relief comes to you. Your patience is only through Allah: it is He who helps you bear it and keeps you steadfast. Do not grieve over those who oppose you and do not respond to your call, and do not be distressed by their plotting and scheming, for it will return upon them as evil and ruin.

Indeed, Allah the Exalted—by His success, His help, His support, and His victory—is with those who fear Him by carrying out what He has commanded and avoiding what He has forbidden, and with those who do good, performing His obligations well, fulfilling their duties toward Him, and adhering to His obedience.
